name: xlide
description: Excel VBA integration for VS Code - tree view, edit VBA modules, AI agent tools

xlide.attachToRunningExcel.description: Windows only: when opening a workbook or running a macro, try to attach to a running Excel instance and reuse an already-open workbook before opening it again.

xlide.excelIntegration.coordinationMode.description: Windows only: what XLIDE does when a workbook is open in Excel (which locks the file) during a module save, F5 Run Macro at Cursor, or Open Workbook. 'block' (default, safest): refuse and ask you to close it in Excel. 'closeTracked': gracefully close the workbook (without saving Excel's stale copy) in Excel instances XLIDE opened, then proceed. 'closeForce': close the workbook in any running Excel, force-quitting Excel if it will not close (unsafe; can lose unsaved work in other open workbooks).

xlide.excelIntegration.trackOpenedWorkbo.description: Windows only: when the coordination mode is 'closeTracked', only close workbooks XLIDE itself opened. Turn off to close a matching workbook in any running Excel instance (including ones you opened manually). Ignored for 'block' and 'closeForce'.

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenAfterClose.description: Windows only: after XLIDE closes a workbook in Excel to write to it under 'closeTracked'/'closeForce' (a module save, add, rename, or delete), reopen the workbook afterward so your Excel view is restored. Turn off to leave it closed until you reopen it yourself. (F5 Run Macro at Cursor always reopens read-only to run, and Open Workbook opens in the mode you picked; neither is affected by this setting.)

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenMode.description: Windows only: how XLIDE reopens a workbook it closed when 'Reopen After Close' is on. 'lastState' (default) puts it back the way it was, so read-only stays read-only and editable stays editable. 'readOnly' always reopens read-only, keeping the file unlocked so the next XLIDE save works. 'readWrite' reopens for editing in Excel, which re-locks the file (the next XLIDE save must close it again). F5 always reopens read-only regardless of this setting.

xlide.excelIntegration.reopenReadOnlyAft.description: Windows only: when a workbook is open READ-ONLY in Excel, a module save still writes the file (a read-only open does not lock it), but Excel keeps showing its older copy. Turn this on to have XLIDE silently close and reopen the read-only workbook in Excel after each save so its view matches the saved file. Only acts when the workbook is actually open read-only in Excel; never reopens a workbook you closed, and never affects a workbook open for editing.

xlide.diagnostics.enabled.description: Show live VBA diagnostics (structural block-balance plus high-confidence semantic checks: unterminated strings, duplicate declarations, assignment to a constant, and the Option Explicit reminder).

xlide.analysis.visibleSeverities.description: Global default analysis finding severities for workbooks that do not define a workbook-specific value for this setting.

xlide.analysis.ruleSeverityOverrides.description: Global default guarded rule severity overrides keyed by analysis rule code. Warning and information rules can be set to 'off'; only rules marked downgrade-safe can be set from error to 'warning'.

xlide.analysis.untrackedRules.description: Global default analysis diagnostic rule codes hidden from tracking for workbooks that do not define a workbook-specific value for this setting.

xlide.editor.blockLayout.description: Controls VBA Smart Enter and block-snippet layout. 'comfy' inserts spacer lines around the editable body; 'compact' places the editable body directly above the closer.

xlide.editor.continueCommentOnNewline.description: When the line above is a VBA comment (starts with an apostrophe), pressing Enter begins the new line with an apostrophe to continue the comment. Turn off for a plain new line with no apostrophe.

xlide.editor.mirrorCommentSpacing.description: When continuing a comment, copy the run of spaces that follows the apostrophe on the line above so the text lines up. Turn off to insert just the apostrophe with no space. Only applies when 'Continue Comment On New Line' is on.

xlide.explorer.autoExpandCollapse.description: Automatically reveal the active module in the XLIDE explorer and collapse the others as you switch editor tabs (a one-workbook, one-module accordion). Turn off to leave the tree as you arrange it - switching tabs and expanding nodes will not auto-collapse anything.

xlide.docs.enabled.description: Enrich VBA hovers and call tips with developer-defined XML documentation: '''-comments above your procedures and external metadata files found in the workspace.

xlide.docs.metadataGlob.description: Glob (relative to each workspace folder) that locates external VBA documentation metadata files. These describe symbols using the same XML vocabulary as '''-comments and override the built-in curated library.

xlide.performance.trace.description: Write slow XLIDE performance trace events to the XLIDE output channel. Recent timings are always available from the Copy Performance Snapshot command.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listWorkbooks
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Finds all Excel workbooks (.xlsm, .xlsb, .xlam) in the current workspace and returns their absolute paths. Call this first when the user has not specified a file path, or when you need to discover which workbooks are available.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_getWorkbookInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a combined one-shot summary of an Excel workbook: VBA modules (name + type), worksheets (name + used dimensions), and named ranges. Treat the workbook/XLIDE virtual modules as the source of truth for VBA. Use this as the first discovery call instead of calling xlide_listModules and xlide_listSheets separately.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_validateWorkbook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks a workbook's VBA project for cross-structure inconsistencies and returns {issues: [...]}. An empty issues array means the project is structurally sound. Use this to audit a workbook before or after edits.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_analyzeWorkbook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Analyzes every VBA module in a workbook using XLIDE's VBA syntax and structural analyzer - the SAME high-confidence, false-positive-free rule engine that powers the live editor diagnostics, letting an agent VERIFY THAT ANALYSIS PASSES IN REAL TIME. Returns a JSON report: {filePath, moduleCount, errorCount, warningCount, problems: [{moduleName, moduleType, line, column, severity, code, message}]}. An empty problems array means the workbook's VBA passes analysis. Use this after writing or editing modules (e.g. after xlide_writeModule) or to audit an entire workbook. Covers block-balance, unterminated strings, duplicate declarations, Const assignment, malformed procedure headers, argument-count mismatches, unbalanced parentheses, Sub/Function-not-defined and more - each carrying an MS-VBAL spec reference. Complements XLIDE's inline ''' XML doc-comments and external *.vbref.xml metadata files, which enrich hovers and call tips for the symbols this analyzer checks.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm (or .xlsb / .xlam) file to analyze

languageModelTools.name: xlide_runVbaTests
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs discovered '@xlide-test' VBA tests in a workbook through XLIDE's production owned read-only Excel test oracle, writes the same timestamped artifacts/status_for_ci.json as the Tests GUI, and returns JSON {ok, summary, artifacts, report}. Use this after editing workbook VBA to verify tests pass without opening the Tests GUI. Requires the workbook to have the current XlideAssert.bas support module installed and Microsoft Excel COM to be available. Supports narrowing by moduleName, procedureName, testIds, includeTags, excludeTags, and failFast. Set includeHostEvents true only when diagnosing host/oracle behavior.

filePath.description: Absolute path to the .xlsm (or .xlsb / .xlam) file to test

moduleName.description: Optional VBA standard module name to restrict discovery

procedureName.description: Optional test Sub procedure name to run

testIds.description: Optional exact XLIDE test ids to run

includeTags.description: Optional tags; when present, only tests with at least one matching tag run

excludeTags.description: Optional tags to exclude from the run

failFast.description: Stop after the first failed, timed out, host-error, or unexpected-pass result

includeHostEvents.description: Include low-level Excel host oracle events in the JSON response for debugging

languageModelTools.name: xlide_createWorkbook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates a new macro-enabled workbook (.xlsm or .xlsb) with an empty VBA project (ThisWorkbook, Sheet1, Module1) at the given absolute path. Fails if the file already exists; it never overwrites an existing workbook. Use this to start a fresh workbook before adding modules or cell data.

filePath.description: Absolute path for the new .xlsm (or .xlsb) file

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listModules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all VBA modules from the live Excel workbook/XLIDE structure. Returns module names and types (standard, class, document). Use this before reading or editing workbook VBA; do not infer module state from exported .bas/.cls repo files, which can be stale, unless the user explicitly asks to work on those export artifacts.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listSubs
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all Sub and Function procedures in a specific VBA module. Returns procedure names, kinds (Sub/Function/Property Get/Let/Set), and line numbers.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Canonical way to read workbook VBA source. Reads the full source of a module from the Excel workbook and returns raw VBA text including Attribute declarations. The .xlsm/.xlsb is a binary container, not text - always read VBA through this tool or through the XLIDE virtual file system (modules opened from the XLIDE tree are live workbook documents at xlide-vba:// URIs), never by opening the workbook file directly. Do not read exported .bas/.cls/.frm files in the project as a substitute, even when they look current: they are one-way artifacts and can be stale. Read those only when the user explicitly asks about the export artifacts themselves.

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to read

languageModelTools.name: xlide_writeModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Canonical way to edit workbook VBA. Writes VBA source directly into the Excel workbook and saves automatically. The .xlsm/.xlsb is a binary OOXML container, so VBA changes persist only through this tool or through the XLIDE virtual file system: modules opened from the XLIDE tree are live workbook documents at xlide-vba:// URIs, and saving one writes into the workbook. Never edit the workbook file with generic file/text tools, and do not write exported .bas/.cls/.frm files in the project as a way of changing VBA - those are one-way artifacts that no workbook reads back, so editing one changes nothing. Touch them only when the user explicitly asks. Creates the module if it does not exist (optionally pass kind='class'; default is standard). IMPORTANT: Use only ASCII characters to avoid character mangling - no Unicode, emoji, or accented characters.

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to write

source.description: The full VBA source code to write into the module

languageModelTools.name: xlide_renameModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Renames a VBA module in an Excel workbook and saves the file. Operates on the live XLIDE module - do not rename the .xlsm/.xlsb or its exported .bas/.cls files to rename a module. Use this to change a module's name. After renaming, any references to the old name in other modules must be updated manually with xlide_writeModule.

moduleName.description: Current name of the VBA module

newName.description: New name for the VBA module

languageModelTools.name: xlide_deleteModule
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Permanently deletes a VBA module from an Excel workbook and saves the file. Operates on the live XLIDE module - do not delete the .xlsm/.xlsb or its exported .bas/.cls files to remove a module. This cannot be undone. Only delete standard or class modules; avoid deleting document modules (Sheet/ThisWorkbook).

moduleName.description: Name of the VBA module to delete

languageModelTools.name: xlide_listSheets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists all worksheet names and their used cell ranges (dimensions) in an Excel file. Call this first whenever the sheet name is unknown before using xlide_readCells, xlide_readFormulas, or xlide_writeCells. Returns an array of {name, dimensions} objects where dimensions is in A1 notation (e.g. 'A1:D20') or empty for a blank sheet.

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads computed cell values (not formulas) from a worksheet in an Excel file. Returns a 2D array of values (rows x columns). If the sheet name is unknown, call xlide_listSheets first. To read raw formulas instead, use xlide_readFormulas.

range.description: Cell range in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1:D10'

languageModelTools.name: xlide_readFormulas
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads raw cell content including formula strings (e.g. '=SUM(A1:A10)') from a worksheet. Use this instead of xlide_readCells when you need to understand or reproduce spreadsheet logic. Returns a 2D array; formula cells contain the formula string, non-formula cells contain their value.

range.description: Cell range in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1:D10'

languageModelTools.name: xlide_writeCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Writes values to a range of cells in a worksheet in an Excel file. The file is saved automatically. If the sheet name is unknown, call xlide_listSheets first. IMPORTANT: Use only ASCII characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and standard ASCII punctuation) to avoid character mangling. Avoid Unicode, emoji, accented characters, and special symbols.

startCell.description: Top-left cell in A1 notation, e.g. 'A1'

data.description: 2D array of values to write (rows of columns)

languageModelTools.name: xlide_exportModules
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Exports all VBA modules from an Excel VBA workbook to a folder using <workbook>.xlide_settings.json behavior shared with UI commands. This is a sync/export operation, not the primary agent editing surface: read and write workbook code through xlide_readModule/xlide_writeModule unless the user explicitly asks to manage exported repo files. Uses live module reads from the workbook. Supports exportMode exportAll (default: export every module, no deletes) and trueUp (export every module, then remove stale .bas/.cls module files missing from the workbook).

exportFolder.description: Optional absolute folder path. If omitted, uses the workbook-specific exportFolder from <workbook>.xlide_settings.json

exportMode.description: Optional mode override for this run

languageModelTools.name: xlide_configureExportMode
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets the persistent workbook-specific exportMode in <workbook>.xlide_settings.json beside the Excel VBA workbook. Use exportAll by default unless the user explicitly asks to delete stale .bas/.cls module files missing from the workbook.

exportMode.description: Persistent workbook-specific export mode to store in <workbook>.xlide_settings.json
